cards.explanation: The answer is that each division took its own month. The divisions were on rotating military duty each month throughout the year, and each one had 24,000 men (1 Chronicles 27:1). Twelve divisions, twelve months, and everybody knew when their turn came. I wish my kitchen ran that smooth, friends. My oven schedule is basically vibes.

The answer is men aged twenty or under. "David did not count the men aged twenty or under…" (1 Chronicles 27:23). So the census had a line drawn right there at twenty. The text gives us that one group and nothing more, so I'm not going to make up extra rules for it.

The answer is that the LORD said Israel would be as many as the stars. The text says David left them out "…because the LORD had said that He would make Israel as numerous as the stars of the sky." (1 Chronicles 27:23). The reason comes straight from the text, so I don't have to guess. Funny thing, friends, I know a little about stars myself, since mine light up every time a cookie box is sealed.

The answer is False. The text says Joab son of Zeruiah "…began to count the men but did not finish." (1 Chronicles 27:24). He got going, and then the count was left unfinished. I've started plenty of batches I didn't finish, friends, but nobody wrote it in a chronicle.

The word is wrath. "For because of this census wrath came upon Israel…" (1 Chronicles 27:24). It's a heavy line, so I'll just say it plainly and leave it there. The text tells us what came, and I won't add a reason it doesn't give.

The answer is True. The text says "…the number was not entered in the Book of the Chronicles of King David." (1 Chronicles 27:24). So that count never made it into the record. I'd call that a very short entry, friends.
